---
title: Share links
description: Send someone a link that plays one private video on a page ClipMux hosts, and revoke it when you're done.
---

A share link is a URL like `https://video.example.com/s/…` that plays one
video for anyone who has it, with no sign-in and no app of yours in the
way. Use it to send a draft to a client, or a lesson to someone outside
your platform. Each link can expire, you can revoke it at any time, and you
can see how many views it had.

Each link owns its own signed playback ID, made with it. Revoking the link
revokes that ID and nothing else: your app's playback ID and other links
keep playing.

## Before you start

- A video. It can still be processing; the page waits for it.
- An API key with `assets:write` to create and revoke links, and
  `assets:read` to list them. The default scopes have both.

## Create a link

<Tabs items={['Node', 'curl']}>
<Tab value="Node">

```ts
import { ClipMux } from '@clipmux/node'

const clipmux = new ClipMux()
const share = await clipmux.shares.create('ast_…', {
  name: 'For the client', // optional, one line, up to 100 characters
  expires_at: '2026-12-31T23:59:59Z', // optional; leave it out for a link that never expires
})
console.log(share.url) // https://video.example.com/s/…
```

</Tab>
<Tab value="curl">

```bash
curl -s https://video.example.com/v1/assets/ast_…/shares \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLIPMUX_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name": "For the client", "expires_at": "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z"}'
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

`POST /v1/assets/{id}/shares` answers `201`:

```json
{
  "id": "shr_…",
  "asset_id": "ast_…",
  "name": "For the client",
  "url": "https://video.example.com/s/…",
  "playback_id": "pid_…",
  "status": "active",
  "expires_at": "2026-12-31T23:59:59Z",
  "created_at": "2026-11-18T09:00:00Z"
}
```

`url` is what you send. `expires_at` must be in the future, and it can't be
changed later: to extend a link, make a new one. The link's playback ID
shows in the video's `playback_ids` with `share: {id, name}`.

You can also make links in the dashboard: open the video under **Videos**,
then **Share links** and **New share link**.

## What the recipient sees

The link opens a page on your ClipMux server. It shows the video's title,
`<clipmux-player>` with the video's subtitles and chapters, and a small
"Shared with ClipMux" credit, and nothing else.

- While the video is processing, the page says so and checks again every
  15 seconds.
- Once the link expires or is revoked, or the video is deleted, the page
  says the link doesn't work and asks them to get a new one from whoever
  shared it. A viewer who is watching when that happens is stopped.
- The page renews its own tokens, so a long video plays to the end.
- The page can't be put in an iframe, asks search engines not to index it,
  and sends no referrer.

The page keeps a random viewer ID in the browser's storage, so your
analytics count unique viewers. A private window sends none.

## List links and their views

```ts
const links = await clipmux.shares.list('ast_…')
// [{ id, name, url, status, expires_at, views_30d, … }], newest first
```

`GET /v1/assets/{id}/shares` lists every link of the video, with
`views_30d`, its views over the last 30 UTC days. A link's views also count
in the video's [analytics](/docs/build/analytics), though ClipMux signs its
tokens.

`status` is one of:

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `active` | The link plays. |
| `revoked` | You revoked it, or the video was deleted. |
| `expired` | Its `expires_at` has passed. |

## Revoke a link

```ts
await clipmux.shares.delete('shr_…')
```

`DELETE /v1/shares/{id}` revokes the link's playback ID. It answers `200`
once the ID is unpublished and `202` while it is being revoked. Revoking a
link twice changes nothing.

An expired link stops at its expiry by itself; within a minute ClipMux also
revokes its playback ID.

## Play a link in another player

The share page is for people with a browser. For a player that can't open
a page, such as a TV app or a media player, get a signed `master.m3u8` URL
for the link:

```ts
const { url, expires_at } = await clipmux.shares.streamUrl('shr_…')
```

`POST /v1/shares/{id}/stream-url` answers `{url, expires_at}`. The URL
can't renew itself: it lasts until the link's expiry or the server's
longest token lifetime, whichever comes first, and stops when the link is
revoked. It answers `409 share_expired`, `409 share_revoked`, or `409
asset_not_ready` while the video is processing.

## Check it works

Open `share.url` in a private window. The video plays with no sign-in.

```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' \
  "https://video.example.com/s/$SECRET/playback"
```

`$SECRET` is the last part of the link's URL. This is what the page asks
for each token:

- `200`: the link plays.
- `409 asset_not_ready`: the video is still processing.
- `404 share_not_found`: the link was revoked, its video deleted or its app
  disabled.
- `410 share_expired`: the link has expired.
